key_insight: The paper shows that the best amount of reference guidance is not determined by continuation success alone; it depends on a tradeoff between generating a different correct trajectory and the surprisal of the reference suffix.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive Reference Guidance (ARG) gives a practical way to build verified trajectories within a fixed generation budget, improving training efficiency for reasoning RL.
method: Use prefix continuation: start from a verified reference prefix and let the model continue.
Keep the model’s continuation only if it passes verification; otherwise fall back to the reference trajectory.
Learn a shared prefix selector from continuation outcomes, then apply ARG in GRPO on all-failure groups.
evidence_signal: Across five mathematical reasoning benchmarks with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, ARG achieved the highest aggregate pass@12 among evaluated methods with competitive average sampled accuracy.
watch_item: ARG still depends on verification and a careful prefix-selection policy, so its gains may be sensitive to the choice of verifier and the fixed generation budget.
paper_title: Balancing Reference Guidance and Free Generation in Trajectory Rollouts for Reasoning RL
